messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>

Subject: Dedicated pool stewardship request: temporary slice & autoscale waiver

Team —

Heads-up / ask for the week of Dec 27 – Jan 7 (holiday sprint window). Orca Health is moving a live pilot that will require sustained low-latency throughput for an internal clinical POC. They are asking for a small dedicated slice to ensure reliable tail latency while their client-facing flows run.

High-level ask:
- Temporary dedicated slice: ~4x A100-equivalent GPU slots for 12 continuous days (27 Dec – 7 Jan inclusive).
- Autoscale waiver: allow controlled burst above standard pool quotas for the slice during peak hours (expected 18:00–22:00 PST) with preemption fallback.
- Fast turnaround: we need an ops + product decision and a runbook before the 24th so Orca can schedule integration testing.

Questions for you:
- Kimberly — what commercial guardrails do we require for a short-term carveout (billing cadence, overage rules, credits)?
- Jonas — what infra work is needed to make a temporary reservation + burst factor available safely (scheduling, preemption window, canary plan)?
- Marissa — anything from the pilot onboarding / customer success side we should lock before committing?

I attached the proposed playbook template (reservation-playbook-v1.docx) — please review, and if we can agree on the risk controls I’ll confirm with Orca today. If helpful, I can set a 30-min sync tomorrow morning (09:30 PT).

Thanks —
Grace
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.com
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 08:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool stewardship request: temporary slice & autoscale waiver

Grace —

Thanks for the clear framing. Short answers up front: we can support a time-limited carveout, but we should define (1) exact billing terms, (2) preemption SLAs, and (3) an explicit handback process.

Initial commercial guardrails I propose:
- Billing: hourly metered for the carveout window, invoiced on the next regular billing cycle. If the customer requests a refund for reliability issues, credits limited to the carveout hours only (no blanket credits).
- Overage: any sustained use beyond the agreed slice will be billed at standard reserved overage rates; override requires written approval.
- Credits/discount: for pilot customers we can offer a one-time 10% pilot discount but require sign-off from Sales Ops (Marissa can you confirm approval path?).

Operational conditions we should enforce (to reduce risk):
- Preemption window: 10 minutes notice before evicting non-carveout jobs.
- Canary phase: first 24 hours limited to 50% of burst capacity.
- Monitoring: we require synthetic QPS + tail-latency checks attached to the reservation with automated rollback if SLOs degrade by >20%.

I reviewed the attached playbook and left a few inline comments (see reservation-playbook-v1.docx). If we agree on the above, I can draft the amendment text for the pilot and circulate to Finance/Sales Ops.

Kimberly
Head of Sales Operations
kimberly_park@redwood.com
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool stewardship request: temporary slice & autoscale waiver

Thanks — tagging on infra constraints and a short implementation plan.

Current state:
- The dedicated A100-equivalent pool is at ~72% avg utilization this month with peaks up to 88% in evening windows.
- Default autoscaler enforces a hard per-tenant cap and preemption policy that favors burst latency SLOs only for Reserved contracts.

What we need to enable the carveout safely:
1) Temporary reservation object scoped to Orca pilot (start/end dates) with reservation metadata. Implementation: create reservation row + allocate affinity labels to nodes. Effort: 4–6 hours config + 1 small DB migration to track temporary reservations.
2) Burst parameter: add a max_burst_factor flag (allowed up to 1.5x for pilot) and a preemption grace period (10m). Effort: change autoscaler config and a controlled rollout — ~1 day for code + 1 day for rollout/testing.
3) Canary: run a small synthetic load against the slice for 3 hours on day 1, monitor tail p99 latency and eviction events. We’ll keep quantized fallback models ready to route traffic if latency moves beyond threshold.

Attached is a quick simulation I ran with a conservative traffic shape — dedicated-reserve-sim.csv (columns: timestamp, allocated_slots, pool_util, estimated_tail_ms). Notable: with a 1.5x burst, tail p99 stays < 320ms under the simulated pattern but pool utilization would touch 95% at the peak, which increases eviction risk for non-reserved jobs.

Rollout timeline (earliest):
- Config + migration: 2026-12-23 (day)
- Canary run + monitoring tuning: 2026-12-24 (overnight)
- Final handoff / activation: 2026-12-27 morning (aligns with customer ask)

Risk controls we should lock into the playbook: 1) auto-evict non-reserved jobs with 10m notice, 2) auto-rollback the burst flag if eviction rate > 3% in any 1h window, 3) manual ops approval to extend beyond 7 days.

Jonas
Director, Infrastructure
jonas_weber@redwood.com

- Commercial terms: Kimberly to prepare the pilot amendment with a one-time 10% pilot discount and explicit overage/credit definitions. Marissa, please route to Sales Ops / Finance for sign-off by EOD 12/23.

Action owners:
